figures.name: se-gol · Segol
figures.notationEvidence: Printed p30: initial G4 quarter shared; four upper-stem eighths G4/F4/A4/G4. The lower-stem C4/A4 eighths and F4 quarter form the separate alternative, sharing the A4 head. Neither line is played as harmony.

figures.name: Munach · before four printed signs
figures.contextPending: The four source glyphs are retained in the image; a modern sign predicate is not inferred.

figures.name: Munach · before Mahpakh
figures.notationEvidence: Printed p31: B-flat4 quarter; C5 normal eighth; only the following B-flat4/A4/G4 have the secondary beam and form a sixteenth-note 3:2 triplet. C5/A4 normal eighths follow, then a quarter rest. The slur starts at the first C5 and ends at the final A4. Staff lines are not counted as beams. Four quarter beats without padding.

figures.name: Munach · before Mercha / Tevir
figures.notationEvidence: Printed p31: F4 quarter; beamed B-flat4/A4/G4 eighth-note triplet; G4 half. Smaller arc joins identical G4 heads (tie); the longer arc starts at B-flat4 (slur). No extra attack at the tied half note.

figures.name: Mahpach → paschto → sokef koton
figures.notationEvidence: Printed p31 6/8: A4 eighth pickup shared. Upper line: D4/F4/F4/C5/A4/A4 eighths, then A4/F4/F4/G4/F4 eighths. Lower line: C4/F4/F4 eighths, A4 quarter/F4 eighth, then A4/F4/F4 eighths/F4 quarter. Six quarter beats per route, including the pickup; the final source segment is not padded to a full6/8bar. The six common physical heads keep their identities. PrefaceIX defines doubled non-Chor lines as alternative melodies; they are never combined.

figures.name: Paschto koton · auf einem Worte
figures.contextPending: The printed condition says on one word; its modern accent predicate is not inferred.

figures.name: Paschto koton · after printed predecessors
figures.pending: A small slashed component and its relation to the adjacent beamed notes need literal grace/alternative interpretation; no duration is invented.

figures.name: Poser · Pazer
figures.pending: A small unmeasured grace component occurs inside the source melisma; source ornament/timing treatment still needs explicit evidence.

figures.name: T’lischo k’ta-noh
figures.pending: Three small beamed components occur between a plain principal note and the following main note. Their grace-size relationship and timing need explicit interpretation; no regular32nd duration is assigned.

figures.name: T’lischo g’do-loh
figures.notationEvidence: Printed p33: leading sixteenth rest and F4 sixteenth/eighth/dotted-eighth/sixteenth/quarter prefix. The ending is F4 dotted eighth, G4 sixteenth, A4 eighth, G4/F4/G4/F4 sixteenths. The lower slur runs from the first ending F4 to its final F4. No meter padding is supplied.

figures.name: Dargo → t’wir
figures.notationEvidence: Printed p34: F4 sixteenth prefix; C5 eighth and B-flat4/A4/G4/F4 sixteenths; A4/G4 eighths; sixteenth rest. The next sixteenth has alternative G4/D4 heads. Tevir continues D4 quarter, C4/D4 sixteenths, F4 eighth. No simultaneous chord or invented pause is supplied.

figures.name: Mercho → tipcho → sof po-suk · printed ending
figures.notationEvidence: Printed p35: F4 eighth pickup; C5 quarter/F4 eighth, G4 dotted eighth with F4/E4/D4 sixteenths. Only two beams span those three descending notes; the top staff line is not a third beam. The next A4 quarter is followed by two distinct eighth rests, D4/A4 sixteenths and A4/F4 eighths. The final dotted-quarter A4 or G4 heads are alternatives under prefaceIX, followed by a common D4 quarter and eighth rest. Both final source heads participate in the printed closing phrase arc; physical head-specific endpoint interpretation awaits independent review. Ten quarter beats per route, preserving three distinct rests and source extents without meter padding.

figures.name: Schalscheles · first rare-sign setting
figures.pending: Literal component transcription is not yet complete; no notes are supplied.

figures.name: Karne poroh / jerach ben jomo · joint source example
figures.pending: Printed heading order and modern reader accent order differ; actual example underlay must be checked independently.

figures.name: Mercho k’fuloh · first rare-sign setting
figures.notationEvidence: Printed p36 first setting: B-flat4 dotted eighth/A4 sixteenth/G4 dotted eighth/A4 sixteenth/B-flat4 dotted eighth/C5 sixteenth, followed by D5/C5/A4 quarters and C5/B-flat4/G4 quarters. Preserve the outer slur and both nested three-note slurs. The printed example text is documentary; automatic Hebrew underlay remains unassigned.

scope: Complete 32-cell first-setting inventory; 27 source figures have literal pitch and written-value transcriptions. Four figures have explicit alternatives, giving 31 single-figure routes. Five source cells remain pending. No arbitrary-word fitting or complete melody grammar is supplied.
timing: Written note/rest values at an independently chosen quarter-note tempo. Printed recitative/bar separators do not impose inferred measure counts, breaths or expressive durations. Source leading, interior, dotted and final rests are retained. The two retained fermatas have unspecified hold lengths; instrumental playback uses their written values, without an inferred extension.

applicationIssue.status: Preserve both source and reader. Do not infer component-to-word alignment from horizontal heading order.

limits: Source figures only. No complete contextual melody system, regional identity for 1.W., Kinnor equivalence, pronunciation transformation, Hebrew syllable fitting or new singing voice is asserted. Existing text, accents, notes, source audio and timing data remain unchanged.

notationPrinciple.literalGerman: Ebenso sind die doppelten Notenreihen auf einem Liniensystem nur als zwei verschiedene Weisen zu betrachten, wenn sie nicht mit „Chor“ bezeichnet sind.
notationPrinciple.english: Two note lines on a single staff are to be treated as two different melodies unless marked Chor.
notationPrinciple.application: The Segol stem-lines, Darga heads, Mahpakh/Pashta/Zaqef stem-lines and two initial Sof heads in the printed ending are explicit alternatives. Each route is monophonic; source alternatives are never superimposed or merged. Shared physical heads keep the same component IDs. Adaptation/translation/musical review remain pending.
